title: Northbridge Finance - Private VPC Discovery
topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway
Security controls: KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML
summary: Discovery focused on Northbridge's network constraints and compliance requirements for a Private VPC deployment. Main concerns: cross-account peering, IP space, private endpoints (PrivateLink/ENIs), region availability, and key management. SE to run feasibility runbook + perf benchmark. Next: share security docs, network diagram, and schedule technical deep-dive.
next_steps: Send Redwood security / SOC2 docs (Sophie) - by 2027-10-22
Customer to share VPC CIDR + network diagram (Aaron) - by 2027-10-25
Schedule SE-led technical deep-dive to validate Transit Gateway connectivity (Marco) - week of 2027-10-26
Run a short perf benchmark in their dev VPC / pilot cluster (Redwood + Aaron) - kickoff 2027-11-01
action_items: Owner: Sophie | Item: Share SOC2 report, private deployment checklist, and example network templates | Due: 2027-10-22
Owner: Aaron | Item: Export & share current VPC CIDRs, route tables, peering attachments, and security group baseline | Due: 2027-10-25
Owner: Marco | Item: Prepare Transit Gateway / PrivateLink feasibility notes and list of required IAM roles | Due: 2027-10-26
Owner: Leila | Item: Confirm KMS/HSM requirements and whether a customer-managed key is mandatory | Due: 2027-10-27
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Tran: Thanks everyone for joining, appreciate it. We're gonna run through your private VPC needs and the network stuff, and Marco from our SE team will jump in for the deep bits.
[00:14] David Chen: Hey Sophie, yeah thanks. We're mostly trying to understand how Redwood's private offering would sit inside our AWS org, specifically cross-account peering, IP footprint, and region availability.
[00:28] Sophie Tran: Totally. Quick intros — Marco is our solutions engineer, he runs the private deploys and the networking playbook.
[00:35] Marco Diaz: Hi all, hi David, Leila, Aaron. I'll try to keep it practical — we've done a number of setups with transit gw, private link, VPC peering.
[00:45] Aaron Patel: Quick context: we run EKS clusters in us-east-1 and us-west-2, some data plane in eu-west-1 for redundancy. We have strict CIDR ranges — 10.0.0.0/16 used heavily, so IP consumption is a real constraint.
[01:02] Leila Morgan: From security, SOC2 is fine but we need audit logs forwarded, SAML SSO, and customer-managed KMS keys for any sensitive model artifacts. Also data residency in EU for some product lines.
[01:18] Sophie Tran: Understood. High level, Redwood Private offers a control plane that can be in Redwood-managed account or a customer-managed control plane — we support VPC peering or PrivateLink-style private endpoints, and we can do dedicated capacity if you want GPU isolation.
[01:36] David Chen: When you say PrivateLink-style, is that AWS PrivateLink / Interface endpoints, or do you use ENIs in our VPC?
[01:44] Marco Diaz: Good question. We have two common patterns: 1) Interface endpoints / PrivateLink where our service exposes an NLB-backed endpoint in our account and you create an interface endpoint, or 2) a peered VPC where we deploy worker ENIs into a customer VPC via a dedicated account, depending on compliance. PrivateLink keeps traffic within AWS but requires ENI quota and subnets per AZ.
[02:05] Aaron Patel: ENI limits are a problem for us — we already spike close to limits in some subnets. How do you handle scaling?
[02:13] Marco Diaz: If ENI limits are tight, we recommend Transit Gateway with routing to a shared services VPC or a dedicated VPC with NAT'd workers — less ENI pressure but more lateral routing. Transit GW also helps if you need many-to-many connections across accounts/regions.
[02:29] Leila Morgan: And audit logs — we need CloudTrail and VPC flow logs forwarded to our Splunk/ELK. Can Redwood ship logs to our S3 bucket or do you ingest?
[02:40] Sophie Tran: We can forward logs to your S3 or support a push to your logging collector. For Private deployments we typically deliver an artifacts package and a config that sets up CloudTrail trails to your bucket and an optional Kinesis/Firehose path. We'll include audit pipeline docs.
[02:55] David Chen: Region constraints — we need inference close to our EKS clusters in us-east-1 for latency-sensitive features, but some regulated workloads must run in eu-west-1. Can you support multi-region private deployments?
[03:09] Marco Diaz: Yes, we can deploy model-serving clusters in multiple regions. Two deployment options: separate private deployments per region, or a single control plane with region-specific workers. Both have tradeoffs — separate deployments give stronger data isolation but require more ops overhead.
[03:27] Aaron Patel: Cost-wise, what's the delta between hosted and private? Our leadership will want a TCO estimate — we need rough numbers to justify network work.
[03:36] Sophie Tran: Hosted is pay-as-you-go — lower upfront but per-token costs. Dedicated and Private have reserved capacity options; Private typically has a platform licensing component plus infra. We'll send a TCO template — can do a model comparing per-token hosted vs reserved GPU hourly cost plus networking egress.
[03:53] Leila Morgan: KMS — can we supply our CMK? Mandatory?
[03:57] Marco Diaz: You can definitely supply a customer-managed key (CMK). For private deployments it's common; we support both Redwood-managed keys or CMKs, and integration with HSM partners if you need FIPS/HSM.
[04:08] David Chen: On peering, we have strict central networking — everything must go via our Transit Gateway and central firewall VPC. How do you connect if you require service endpoints in our account?
[04:20] Marco Diaz: We connect via either: 1) Add a Transit Gateway attachment from Redwood account into your Transit GW, or 2) you peer to our dedicated worker VPC and traffic flows through the Transit GW depending on routing. We'll need your networking team to confirm if attachments from third-party accounts are permitted.
[04:36] Aaron Patel: We usually don't allow third-party TGW attachments without a partner review. That might push us toward interface endpoints or a sidecar pattern.
[04:44] Sophie Tran: Noted. If attachments are restricted, PrivateLink/Interface endpoints are the conservative approach. The tradeoff is you need subnets per AZ and ENI quota, and there can be per-GB data charges.
[04:58] David Chen: IP planning — our prod VPC CIDR is 10.0.0.0/16, staging 10.1.0.0/16. If you deploy workers in our VPC, what's the recommended CIDR mapping?
[05:10] Marco Diaz: We usually ask customers to reserve a /20 or /21 block for Redwood workers to avoid collision — depends on expected pod density and per-ENI IP usage. If you can't spare that, we can host in a peered VPC and NAT traffic back.
[05:24] Leila Morgan: Compliance question — do you support isolated control plane inside customer VPC?
[05:29] Marco Diaz: Yes, for high-compliance customers we offer a private control plane option that runs in your account; that gives max isolation and you keep full control of the network and keys. It's a heavier lift to deploy.
[05:40] Aaron Patel: About ephemeral KV cache and checkpointing — where does that live? We don't want model context leaking into other customers.
[05:49] Marco Diaz: Data plane state (KV cache) is isolated per deployment/tenant. For private deployments, the KV cache can reside on local NVMe attached to the instance or in your managed Redis inside your VPC. We can configure prefix caching to reduce duplication. Also we scrub logs and provide retention controls.
[06:05] David Chen: Any gotchas with EKS networking or service meshes? We run Istio in prod.
[06:12] Marco Diaz: Istio can intercept traffic, so you'll need policies to allow the inference worker traffic to the internal endpoints. We recommend CNI-aware deployments and making sure your egress rules don't break internal health checks. We'll provide an EKS integration guide.
[06:26] Sophie Tran: Quick aside, do you have expected QPS and latency SLOs? That helps us size the pilot.
[06:32] David Chen: For our real-time assistant, 95th perc latency under 200ms for short prompts, QPS around 50 sustained during peak. For batch analytics models latency is not critical.
[06:42] Marco Diaz: For 200ms SLOs we generally run inference in-region with GPU-backed instances, and rely on batching/kv-caching to keep token latency low. We'll propose a benchmark config.
[06:54] Leila Morgan: If we do a pilot, can we use a staging VPC with tighter controls?
[06:59] Sophie Tran: Absolutely — staging is the preferred path. We'll do a small pilot in staging to validate connectivity, IAM, KMS, and perf, then expand.
[07:07] Aaron Patel: On IAM, what roles need to exist? We can't hand over broad permissions.
[07:12] Marco Diaz: Minimal roles: an IAM role for Redwood's deployment runner with limited EC2/EKS and networking permissions, and an S3 write role for log export. We'll share least-priv policy templates.
[07:23] David Chen: Ok, procurement — any enterprise contract terms around data residency and indemnity we should expect?
[07:29] Sophie Tran: Standard enterprise contract with data residency clauses, we can include carve-outs for EU-only data, and we have SOC2/ISO attestations. Legal usually asks for liability limits similar to other vendors. We'll loop in Legal once you want to proceed.
[07:42] Leila Morgan: One more — can we restrict model downloads or quantization artifacts from leaving our VPC?
[07:48] Marco Diaz: Yes, we support air-gapped on-prem packages if needed, or a customer-managed artifact store in your account. For most PrivateVPC customers we keep weights in a customer S3 behind VPC endpoints.
[07:59] Sophie Tran: Cool. Recap and next steps — Sophie to share SOC2 and network templates; Aaron to share CIDR and diagram; Marco to prepare TGW/PrivateLink notes and benchmark plan; Leila to confirm KMS requirement.
[08:15] David Chen: Sounds good, we'll try get the diagram to you by Monday.
[08:20] Aaron Patel: Yeah I'll export the VPC layout and send it.
[08:24] Sophie Tran: Great — we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the SE deep-dive. Thanks everyone.
[08:28] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional word swaps present — 'KV cash' appears sometimes instead of 'KV cache', 'Redwood Dedicate' appears once in a sentence; speaker labels are accurate though informal.
